title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a handwritten draft on the back of a typed SGA 7 IX page (Néron models / monodromy pairing). The handwriting is unrelated to the typescript: it belongs to the 1976 IHÉS lecture notes on the divided-power de Rham complex. Notation: 𝒳 is a (formal or lifted) scheme over a base; X is probably its reduction. S_k is a coefficient object over k, possibly a divided-power or symmetric algebra or a PD-envelope; its precise meaning is unsure. C^{**} is a double complex, apparently a (divided-power) de Rham-type resolution. H_c^{**}(X) is a cohomology of X; c probably means 'crystalline' rather than 'compact support', but this is unsure. τ_ω is a truncation (degrees below a bound ω), which recurs throughout the notes.

Diagram (1) is a zigzag of maps: τ_ω RΓ(𝒳,S_k) → τ_ω RΓ(𝒳,C^{**}) ← τ_ω C^{**}(X). Grothendieck says he would like both arrows to be isomorphisms 'dans la cat. divisée'. This most plausibly means a quotient (Serre-type localized) category in which 'negligible' objects, e.g. those killed by bounded torsion, are inverted. It could also be the derived category modulo negligible objects. Passing to cohomology, (1') H^{**}(𝒳,S_k) → H^{**}(𝒳,C^{**}) ← H^{**}_c(X) should then have negligible kernel and cokernel. For the 'horizontal filtration' (one of the two filtrations of the double complex) this gives (2'): τ_ω(H^*(𝒳,k) ⊗_k S_k) ≅ τ_ω H^{**}(𝒳,C^{**}) ≅ τ_ω H^{**}_c(X). This is a Künneth or base-change type decomposition of the double-complex cohomology, valid in a truncated range and up to negligibles.

The problem served is comparing de Rham-type cohomology with divided powers to a 'crystalline' cohomology of X up to controlled (negligible) error, in a range of degrees bounded by ω.
errors: No outright error is visible, but this is a wish list ('On voudrait'), not a proof.
The step from 'isomorphism in the quotient category' to 'negligible kernel and cokernel in cohomology' needs the class of negligible objects to be thick (Serre). That is not stated.
The meanings of S_k, C^{**}, ω and 'négligeable' are not defined on this page.

ideas.what: Compare truncated cohomologies of a divided-power de Rham double complex via a zigzag, required to be isomorphisms modulo negligible objects (a quotient category)
ideas.modern_name: Comparison theorems 'up to bounded torsion' / in the isogeny or quotient category, with truncation τ_{<p} as in Fontaine–Messing or Deligne–Illusie
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot–Ogus (isogeny-category crystalline comparisons), Fontaine–Messing, Deligne–Illusie (truncations below p), Bhatt (derived de Rham up to bounded torsion)
ideas.where_published: Not published; the 1976 IHÉS lecture on the divided-power de Rham complex is only documented in archive notes

ideas.what: Degeneration/identification of the double-complex cohomology via the horizontal filtration as H^*(𝒳,k)⊗S_k in a truncated range
ideas.modern_name: Künneth/base-change splitting of a double-complex spectral sequence (degeneration in a range)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the desired divided-power de Rham comparison as an isomorphism in a 'divided' (quotient) category modulo negligible objects, restricted to a truncation τ_ω. This 'comparison up to negligibles in a range of degrees' strategy appears in this unpublished project, which was never written up.
missed.quote: On voudrait que ces deux flèches dans la cat. divisée [...] soient à noyau et conoyau négligeables
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest as an early instance of the 'up to bounded torsion, in low degrees' philosophy later central to integral p-adic Hodge theory and derived de Rham cohomology. The page is too fragmentary to constitute a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: Fragmentary programmatic draft. The idea of comparisons modulo negligibles in a truncated range is suggestive historically, but it is not developed here and is close to later standard techniques.
transcription_corrections: The first diagram is labelled '(1)', not '(2)'; the text below refers to 'les homom. déduits de (1)'.
'ces deux filtrations' is more likely 'ces deux flèches' (the two arrows of diagram (1)).
'des [?] négligeables' is likely 'soient des quasi-isomorphismes' or similar; negligibility is then stated for kernel and cokernel.
'pour le filtr. horizontal, l'[?] iso' is probably 'pour le filtré horizontal, l'iso'.

The first line reads approximately 'En fait, en demandant qu'en quelques degrés...' with strikethroughs. The second line likely involves τ_ω applied to ℝΓ (τ_ω ℝ* τ_ω, i.e. commutation of truncation with ℝΓ).
In (2') the left vertical marker reads '(2')' or '(1'')'; the right arrow is marked as an isomorphism (≀ or 2).
